title: [finding] `check-issue-citations` `enumerateBoard` takes a short walk as the whole board: no `rel="next"` ends it and the highest number seen becomes the frontier (seen once: 126 of 184 pages, 9,160 phantoms)
body:
Filing gate: **① a gate defect with a measured reach**. Finding class **(a)**. `reach:` `node scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs --census`, the report-only census the half-state patrol reads; the blocking diff verdict is affected too, but only on the enumerate strategy, which a diff takes past 400 distinct numbers. Observed once, and not reproduced on an immediate re-run. The code path that allows it is certain.

Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 2 (`session_014EJ1ED8X4MMrT18BhVx4tx`, seat post #18549) from the #20330 dev report `5882580588` (out-of-scope finding 1), with the code read by this seat on `origin/main` `b05743433b`. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happened

At PR #20554's head `a3c14755f8`, one `--census` run read `enumerated (126 pages)` with frontier #13977, and reported **9,160 never-issued phantoms**. A re-run minutes later read `enumerated (184 pages)` with frontier #20551, the true board.

## Why the code allows it

`enumerateBoard` in `scripts/check-issue-citations.mjs` (`:491` on `origin/main` `b05743433b`):
- It pages `issues?state=all&per_page=100&sort=created&direction=asc` until `parseNextLink` returns `null`. A page whose `Link` header is missing or truncated (a proxy or transport hiccup) therefore ends the walk early.
- It sets `frontier: Math.max(...numbers)` from what it saw. A short walk thus lowers the frontier, and every real number above it is classed `never-issued`.
- It raises only on the page cap and on zero numbers. Nothing compares the enumerated frontier with the board's actual newest number.

Its sibling `probeBoard` (`:520`) reads the frontier directly: `issues?state=all&per_page=1&sort=created&direction=desc`. The enumerate strategy has no such cross-check.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

After the walk, read the newest number the way `probeBoard` does. Refuse the run (a read failure, exit 3) when the enumerated maximum falls short of it by more than the numbers created during the walk. Add a self-test case with a stubbed transport that drops the `Link` header midway, which must fail loudly rather than answer.

## Dedupe

A REST listing of the 1,000 most recently updated issues and PRs (down to #19803), grepped locally for `enumerateBoard`, `frontier`, `never-issued` and `phantom`, found nothing that carries this. #20330 (the qualifier grammar, PR #20554) is a different defect in the same script.

Dedupe words: `issue-citations enumerateBoard truncated frontier` · `census never-issued phantom` · `parseNextLink early stop`
